ledger.note: 583: Dvaravati, a network of Mon-speaking polities in central Thailand, first appears in Chinese records. 'Embassies to the Chinese court are recorded in 583'; the first recognition at the Tang court came with the embassy of 638. The page calls it 'a network of early historic polities', not a unified state, and dates its establishment only to 'the 6th century'.

ledger.note: 648: the political centre moves to Lavapura. 'Kalavarnadisharaja founded or refounded the Lavo Kingdom in 648'; 'by the mid-7th century, prominence appears to have shifted to Lavo's Lavapura' (some scholars date the shift to the 10th or 11th century). Lavo's Cliopatria outline also holds the western and eastern centres kept here.

ledger.note: 913: the western valley passes to Suphannabhum. The Suphannabhum page says the state was founded in 877 and became free 'after its suzerain, Nakhon Pathom of Kamalanka, fell to Phetchaburi in 913'. Reading that Nakhon Pathom as Dvaravati's western centre is mine; the Dvaravati page does not date the loss of Nakhon Pathom.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened. The page treats Dvaravati as a network of polities and a cultural sphere (Mon, Buddhist, 6th-11th century), not one state, so the dossier is a simplification: one dot, one shape. Choices: (1) end 949 (Si Thep) instead of the infobox's 11th century, because 946/949 are the last dated Dvaravati-line events and Lavapura after 648 is Lavo's; (2) from 648 only the western and eastern centres are kept, which lie inside Cliopatria's Lavo outline (lavo-kingdom keeps that outline for 648-1394 and starts Lavo in 648, naming dvaravati as predecessor); if the renderer draws both, a gap-filler should clip one; (3) the Isan and lowland Laos sites are culture only; (4) Tou Yuan, absorbed in 647 by Lavo's Kalavarnadisharaja, is not placed by the page. The Dvaravati page's dates for the Khmer takeover (946 Si Thep, 1005 Lavapura) differ from those in lavo-kingdom (1006). The 913 loss of the west is confidence 1. Haripunjaya (750) is named by its dossier as an offshoot; this dossier does not draw it.
